crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Evidence Extraction Tables
children.blurb: Evidence extraction tables are structured summaries used in literature review and evidence synthesis to pull key claims, study designs, populations, interventions, outcomes and effect sizes from individual papers into a comparable grid.

children.name: Weighing the Scientific Consensus
children.blurb: Weighing the scientific consensus means assessing how much agreement exists across published research on a specific question, rather than relying on a single study.

children.name: Questioning Your Own Sources
children.blurb: Questioning your own sources means treating every paper, claim, and model output as provisional until its provenance, method, and conflicts have been checked.

children.name: Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans
children.blurb: Deep research agents and landscape scans automate the early stages of literature review and evidence synthesis, from finding relevant work to mapping how papers, claims, models, tools, and books relate.

children.name: Translating Between Disciplines
children.blurb: Translating between disciplines means taking findings, methods, or terminology from one research field and restating them so they can be used in another.

sections.body: This section covers how artificial intelligence is used to pull evidence out of research literature and combine it into a coherent picture. In practice, AI systems read papers, identify claims, and place them into structured tables so a researcher can compare findings side by side. They also scan large bodies of work to find where agreement exists and where it does not. The site's library currently holds 135 research papers and 11222 claims extracted from those works, which gives a concrete sense of the scale involved. This is not a theoretical promise; it is the actual output of tools that parse text and record what each study asserts.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is strongest at extraction and organization. AI can reliably turn a paper's methods, sample, and main claim into a row in a table, and it can flag when two papers disagree. What remains unsolved is judgment. Weighing a scientific consensus still requires a human to check whether the extracted claims are faithful, whether the studies are comparable, and whether a majority view is actually well supported. Honest limits include missed nuance, errors in parsing complex sentences, and the risk of treating a large number of weak studies as a strong consensus. The tools reduce the time spent finding and arranging evidence, but they do not replace reading the original paper.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader would start with Evidence Extraction Tables to see how raw claims are pulled from papers and made comparable. From there, Weighing the Scientific Consensus explains how to assess whether those claims point in one direction, while Questioning Your Own Sources turns the lens back on the papers themselves and asks what might be wrong with them. Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans covers the broader sweep, where AI is used to map an entire field quickly, and Translating Between Disciplines addresses the harder problem of moving findings across fields that use different terms and assumptions. Together the pages move from single claims to whole bodies of work and then to the boundaries between fields.
